beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: His bonus bought a TV. Mine bought a slice of the companies selling it.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Both got $5,000. Three check-ins, and the last one stings.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: I went straight to the store. Biggest screen they had, plus a sound bar. Bonus, gone in a day.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: I put mine in an index fund. A tiny slice of a whole market of companies, the TV shops included.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Check-in one, after 10 years. At an assumed 7% a year, my bonus is $9,836.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Meanwhile, my TV? Scratched, slow, and nobody wants to buy it.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Check-in two, 20 years in: $19,348. And my money tree is speeding up.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: My TV finally died. Straight into the bin.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Check-in three, 30 years: $38,061. That whole tree grew from one bonus I never touched.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: So that TV never really cost $5,000. It cost Rohan $38,061.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Poor people buy the thing. Rich people buy a piece of the people selling it.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Next bonus? I'm buying the shop, not the screen.
